Strait of Hormuz Status: October 14, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  228 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
14 October 2026 .
Brent $ 106.34 + 0.38 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 BBC reports a container ship was hit by a projectile and sank in the Strait of Hormuz, though The Straits Times says no injuries were reported from two Singapore-registered vessels struck.

02 WSJ reports two Singapore-registered ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz; Reuters reports two ships sank near the strait after projectile strikes.

03 Brent stood at $106.34, up 0.38% over 24 hours, as of 18:13 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the site of intensifying attack activity, with the lead development contested: MarineLink reports a container ship was struck by a projectile and sank, while the Singapore Maritime and Port Authority, per Yahoo News Singapore and The Straits Times, says no injuries were reported from two Singapore-registered ships that were struck. Reuters reports two ships sank near the strait after projectile strikes, and WSJ reports two Singapore-registered ships were attacked. The New York Times reports attacks on ships in the strait have escalated sharply, and The Straits Times reports attacks have reached their highest level since the start of the Iran war, citing security data. Lloyd's List reports a containership sank as attacks on shipping intensified, and The Japan Times reports Iran is shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before the US vote. A products tanker struck by an unknown projectile, reported by UKMTO, remains in the news from an earlier window. The feed indexed 113 headlines in the last 24 hours. Brent stood at $106.34, up 0.38% over 24 hours, as of 18:13 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. As of 18:22 UTC, 145 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
